Job T03: usp_build_fact_premium_earned (tsql), legacy file estate/tsql/T03_usp_build_fact_premium_earned.sql (SHA-256 5fbf16f70c9c202ea4f177ec504f51992cf11022b0d992bc484b0cfa10e93670).
Written and earned premium in EUR per premium transaction.
Invocations, in order: run: AsOfDate=2025-12-31.

Legacy code:
/*==============================================================================
  Job       dw.usp_build_fact_premium_earned
  Purpose   Premium fact for finance: one row per premium transaction, converted
            to EUR at the rate published on or before the booking date, with
            the premium earned as at the reporting date.
  Author    MOD
  Run by    FIN_MONTH_END, after dw.usp_load_dim_policy
  Output    dw.fact_premium_earned (full refresh)

  Change log
    2016-01-11  MOD  Initial version (CR-0904)
    2016-07-04  MOD  Sterling and dollar business converted to EUR (CR-0977)
    2018-03-19  PK   Policy surrogate key and line of business from dim_policy (CR-1290)
    2019-09-30  PK   Daily rate and monthly instalment for the cash-flow model (CR-1510)
    2021-02-15  MOD  First instalment due date for the direct debit file (CR-1618)
    2023-05-08  JMcK Earned percentage for the finance dashboard (INC-2301)
==============================================================================*/
SET NOCOUNT ON;
GO
IF OBJECT_ID(N'dw.fact_premium_earned', N'U') IS NULL
CREATE TABLE dw.fact_premium_earned (
    txn_id                  INT            NOT NULL,
    policy_id               INT            NOT NULL,
    policy_sk               INT            NOT NULL,
    lob_code                VARCHAR(5)     NOT NULL,
    txn_type                VARCHAR(4)     NOT NULL,
    txn_date                DATE           NOT NULL,
    effective_from          DATE           NOT NULL,
    effective_to            DATE           NOT NULL,
    currency                CHAR(3)        NOT NULL,
    amount                  DECIMAL(12,2)  NOT NULL,
    fx_rate                 DECIMAL(18,8)  NOT NULL,
    written_eur             DECIMAL(14,2)  NOT NULL,
    term_days               INT            NOT NULL,
    earned_days             INT            NOT NULL,
    earned_pct              DECIMAL(5,2)   NOT NULL,
    earned_eur              DECIMAL(14,2)  NOT NULL,
    unearned_eur            DECIMAL(14,2)  NOT NULL,
    daily_rate_eur          DECIMAL(12,4)  NOT NULL,
    monthly_instalment_eur  DECIMAL(14,2)  NOT NULL,
    first_due_date          DATE           NOT NULL,
    as_of_date              DATE           NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT pk_dw_fact_premium_earned PRIMARY KEY (txn_id)
);
GO
CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE dw.usp_build_fact_premium_earned
    @AsOfDate DATE
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;

    DECLARE @job_name  VARCHAR(128) = 'dw.usp_build_fact_premium_earned',
            @rows      INT,
            @err_msg   NVARCHAR(4000),
            @err_no    INT;

    BEGIN TRY
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'start', @status = 'STARTED';

        /* Transactions with their EUR rate: EUR as is, other currencies at the
           latest rate on or before the booking date (later row wins on revisions) */
        IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#txn') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #txn;

        SELECT  t.txn_id, t.policy_id, UPPER(RTRIM(t.txn_type)) AS txn_type, t.txn_date,
                t.effective_from, t.effective_to, t.currency, t.amount,
                CAST(1 AS DECIMAL(18,8)) AS fx_rate
        INTO    #txn
        FROM    stg.premium_transactions t WITH (NOLOCK)
        WHERE   t.currency = 'EUR'
          AND   t.txn_date <= @AsOfDate;

        INSERT INTO #txn (txn_id, policy_id, txn_type, txn_date, effective_from, effective_to,
                          currency, amount, fx_rate)
        SELECT  t.txn_id, t.policy_id, UPPER(RTRIM(t.txn_type)), t.txn_date,
                t.effective_from, t.effective_to, t.currency, t.amount, fx.rate_to_eur
        FROM    stg.premium_transactions t WITH (NOLOCK)
        CROSS APPLY (SELECT TOP 1 r.rate_to_eur
                     FROM   stg.fx_rates r WITH (NOLOCK)
                     WHERE  r.currency = t.currency
                       AND  r.rate_date <= t.txn_date
                     ORDER BY r.rate_date DESC, r._row_seq DESC) fx
        WHERE   t.currency <> 'EUR'
          AND   t.txn_date <= @AsOfDate;

        SELECT @rows = COUNT(*) FROM #txn;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'transactions', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;

        /* Days of cover and days earned by the reporting date */
        IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#earn') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #earn;

        SELECT  x.*,
                CAST(ROUND(x.amount * x.fx_rate, 2) AS DECIMAL(14,2)) AS written_eur,
                DATEDIFF(DAY, x.effective_from, x.effective_to) + 1  AS term_days,
                CASE WHEN @AsOfDate < x.effective_from THEN 0
                     WHEN @AsOfDate >= x.effective_to  THEN DATEDIFF(DAY, x.effective_from, x.effective_to) + 1
                     ELSE DATEDIFF(DAY, x.effective_from, @AsOfDate) + 1
                END AS earned_days
        INTO    #earn
        FROM    #txn x;

        BEGIN TRANSACTION;

        TRUNCATE TABLE dw.fact_premium_earned;

        INSERT INTO dw.fact_premium_earned
               (txn_id, policy_id, policy_sk, lob_code, txn_type, txn_date, effective_from,
                effective_to, currency, amount, fx_rate, written_eur, term_days, earned_days,
                earned_pct, earned_eur, unearned_eur, daily_rate_eur, monthly_instalment_eur,
                first_due_date, as_of_date)
        SELECT  e.txn_id,
                e.policy_id,
                p.policy_sk,
                p.lob_code,
                e.txn_type,
                e.txn_date,
                e.effective_from,
                e.effective_to,
                e.currency,
                e.amount,
                e.fx_rate,
                e.written_eur,
                e.term_days,
                e.earned_days,
                e.earned_days * 100 / e.term_days,
                ROUND(e.written_eur * e.earned_days / 365, 2),
                e.written_eur - ROUND(e.written_eur * e.earned_days / 365, 2),
                ROUND(e.written_eur / e.term_days, 4, 1),
                ROUND(e.written_eur / ISNULL(NULLIF(e.term_days / 30, 0), 1), 2),
                DATEADD(MONTH, 1, EOMONTH(e.effective_from)),
                @AsOfDate
        FROM    #earn e
        JOIN    dw.dim_policy p WITH (NOLOCK)
                ON p.policy_id = e.policy_id
               AND p.is_current = 'Y';

        SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;

        COMMIT TRANSACTION;

        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'dw.fact_premium_earned', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'SUCCESS';
    END TRY
    BEGIN CATCH
        IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;

        SELECT  @err_msg = ERROR_MESSAGE(),
                @err_no  = ERROR_NUMBER();

        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'FAILED',
             @message = @err_msg, @error_number = @err_no;
        THROW;
    END CATCH
END;
GO

request.system_prompt:
Translate one legacy T-SQL (SQL Server 2022) job to PySpark 4.2. Your output must reproduce the legacy output EXACTLY, record for record and value for value, bugs included: reconciliation compares every row and column with the legacy engine's own output.

Write one Python module:
- Imports only from pyspark (pyspark.sql, pyspark.sql.functions as F, pyspark.sql.types as T, pyspark.sql.Window), datetime, decimal, math, re, functools and typing.
- Exactly this entry point: def run(spark: SparkSession, inputs: dict[str, DataFrame], params: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, DataFrame]:
- inputs holds every input table by its legacy name in lower case (e.g. "stg.claims"); params holds the parameters as text (e.g. params["AsOfDate"] == "2025-12-31").
- Return a dict from each output's legacy name to a DataFrame with the output's columns. The harness then casts each column to the contract type shown, as the legacy table's insert would (so a decimal(38,6) value stored into decimal(14,2) is rounded half up).
- Never do I/O or reach engine internals: no spark.read, .write, saveAsTable, spark.conf, RDDs, UDFs, .cache(), getattr, eval, open, os or sys. spark.sql, F.expr and selectExpr only with plain string literals (no f-strings).
- Use only constants that appear in the legacy code, the parameters, or a trap card's fix guidance (format patterns, collation names). Never hard-code data values.
- Reproduce every legacy behaviour exactly, including anything that looks like a bug: never fix it. Mark each line that reproduces a suspected bug with a "# LANSH-DEFECT: <what>" comment and list the bug in defects.
- Row order: Spark has none. Wherever the result depends on order (first or last row, a running value, a cursor, NODUPKEY, RETAIN, LAG), sort on the legacy ORDER BY and then _row_seq, which every source table has in its original row order.
- Spark runs with ANSI mode on: overflow and invalid casts raise errors, and a division by zero raises; use try_divide or a guard only where the legacy engine returns NULL.

structured_output.code:
"""T03 dw.usp_build_fact_premium_earned -> PySpark.

Rebuilds dw.fact_premium_earned in full: one row per premium transaction booked
on or before AsOfDate. Each row carries its EUR rate, written and earned premium
in EUR, the daily rate, the monthly instalment and the first due date.

Legacy behaviour reproduced on purpose:
  * Currency / is_current comparisons follow the default SQL Server collation
    (case-insensitive, trailing blanks ignored).
  * Non-EUR transactions with no rate on or before txn_date are dropped (CROSS APPLY).
  * Transactions with no current dim_policy row are dropped (inner JOIN).
  * earned_pct uses integer division; earned_eur divides by 365, not term_days;
    first_due_date = DATEADD(MONTH, 1, EOMONTH(effective_from)).
"""
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql import types as T
from pyspark.sql import Window


def run(spark: SparkSession, inputs: dict[str, DataFrame], params: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, DataFrame]:
    as_of = F.to_date(F.lit(params["AsOfDate"]))

    txn = inputs["stg.premium_transactions"]
    fx = inputs["stg.fx_rates"]
    dim = inputs["dw.dim_policy"]

    # Collation-like key: CI comparison, trailing blanks ignored
    t_ccy_key = F.upper(F.rtrim(F.col("currency")))

    base = txn.where(F.col("txn_date") <= as_of).select(
        F.col("_row_seq").alias("t_seq"),
        "txn_id",
        "policy_id",
        F.upper(F.rtrim(F.col("txn_type"))).alias("txn_type"),
        "txn_date",
        "effective_from",
        "effective_to",
        "currency",
        "amount",
        t_ccy_key.alias("t_ccy_key"),
    )

    # EUR transactions at rate 1
    eur = base.where(F.col("t_ccy_key") == F.lit("EUR")).withColumn(
        "fx_rate", F.lit(1).cast(T.DecimalType(18, 8))
    )

    # Non-EUR: CROSS APPLY TOP 1 rate on or before txn_date (rate_date DESC, _row_seq DESC)
    non_eur = base.where(F.col("t_ccy_key") != F.lit("EUR"))
    rates = fx.select(
        F.upper(F.rtrim(F.col("currency"))).alias("r_ccy_key"),
        F.col("rate_date").alias("r_date"),
        F.col("rate_to_eur").alias("r_rate"),
        F.col("_row_seq").alias("r_seq"),
    )
    joined = non_eur.join(
        rates,
        (non_eur["t_ccy_key"] == rates["r_ccy_key"]) & (rates["r_date"] <= non_eur["txn_date"]),
        "inner",
    )
    w = Window.partitionBy("t_seq").orderBy(F.col("r_date").desc(), F.col("r_seq").desc())
    non_eur_rated = (
        joined.withColumn("_rn", F.row_number().over(w))
        .where(F.col("_rn") == 1)
        .withColumn("fx_rate", F.col("r_rate").cast(T.DecimalType(18, 8)))
        .drop("_rn", "r_ccy_key", "r_date", "r_rate", "r_seq")
    )

    txn_all = eur.unionByName(non_eur_rated).drop("t_seq", "t_ccy_key")

    # #earn
    ef = F.col("effective_from")
    et = F.col("effective_to")
    term_days = F.datediff(et, ef) + F.lit(1)
    earn = (
        txn_all.withColumn(
            "written_eur",
            F.round(F.col("amount") * F.col("fx_rate"), 2).cast(T.DecimalType(14, 2)),
        )
        .withColumn("term_days", term_days.cast(T.IntegerType()))
        .withColumn(
            "earned_days",
            F.when(as_of < ef, F.lit(0))
            .when(as_of >= et, F.datediff(et, ef) + F.lit(1))
            .otherwise(F.datediff(as_of, ef) + F.lit(1))
            .cast(T.IntegerType()),
        )
    )

    pol = dim.where(F.upper(F.rtrim(F.col("is_current"))) == F.lit("Y")).select(
        F.col("policy_id").alias("p_policy_id"),
        F.col("policy_sk"),
        F.col("lob_code"),
    )

    e = earn.join(pol, earn["policy_id"] == pol["p_policy_id"], "inner")

    earned_eur_expr = F.round(F.col("written_eur") * F.col("earned_days") / F.lit(365), 2)  # LANSH-DEFECT: earned premium divides by 365 instead of term_days

    out = e.select(
        F.col("txn_id"),
        F.col("policy_id"),
        F.col("policy_sk"),
        F.col("lob_code"),
        F.col("txn_type"),
        F.col("txn_date"),
        F.col("effective_from"),
        F.col("effective_to"),
        F.col("currency"),
        F.col("amount"),
        F.col("fx_rate"),
        F.col("written_eur"),
        F.col("term_days"),
        F.col("earned_days"),
        F.expr("(earned_days * 100) div term_days").alias("earned_pct"),  # LANSH-DEFECT: integer division truncates earned_pct to a whole percent
        earned_eur_expr.alias("earned_eur"),
        (F.col("written_eur") - earned_eur_expr).alias("unearned_eur"),  # LANSH-DEFECT: unearned derived from the /365 earned amount
        F.expr(
            "CASE WHEN written_eur / term_days >= 0 "
            "THEN floor(written_eur / term_days, 4) "
            "ELSE ceil(written_eur / term_days, 4) END"
        ).alias("daily_rate_eur"),
        F.round(
            F.col("written_eur")
            / F.expr("cast(coalesce(nullif(term_days div 30, 0), 1) as int)"),
            2,
        ).alias("monthly_instalment_eur"),
        F.add_months(F.last_day(F.col("effective_from")), 1).alias("first_due_date"),  # LANSH-DEFECT: DATEADD(MONTH,1,EOMONTH()) keeps day-of-month (Feb 28 -> Mar 28, Apr 30 -> May 30)
        as_of.alias("as_of_date"),
    )

    return {"dw.fact_premium_earned": out}

defects.intended: Decimal division, e.g. e.earned_days * 100.0 / e.term_days, rounded to 2 places.
defects.title: Integer division in earned_pct
defects.what_it_does: e.earned_days * 100 / e.term_days is int/int, so the value is cut to a whole percent (e.g. 33.00 instead of 33.33) before it is stored in DECIMAL(5,2).

defects.intended: ROUND(written_eur * earned_days / term_days, 2), with unearned = written - earned.
defects.title: Earned premium divides by 365 instead of term_days
defects.what_it_does: earned_eur = ROUND(written_eur * earned_days / 365, 2). Any term other than 365 days is pro-rated wrongly. Terms over 365 days earn more than written, so unearned_eur goes negative. Short terms are under-earned.

defects.intended: A consistent due date: either the end of the following month, EOMONTH(effective_from, 1), or the first of the following month, DATEADD(DAY, 1, EOMONTH(effective_from)).
defects.title: First due date from DATEADD(MONTH,1,EOMONTH())
defects.what_it_does: Adds one month to the month-end date. DATEADD keeps the day number, so when the month has fewer than 31 days the result is not a month end: Feb 28 -> Mar 28, Apr 30 -> May 30, Jun 30 -> Jul 30, Sep 30 -> Oct 30, Nov 30 -> Dec 30.

structured_output.notes:
1. Collation: the currency and is_current comparisons are matched on UPPER(RTRIM(..)). This assumes the database uses the default case-insensitive collation (CI_AS); please confirm. The currency value written out is the raw source value.
2. Rows dropped without a message, as the legacy job does: non-EUR transactions with no rate on or before txn_date (CROSS APPLY) and transactions with no current dim_policy row (inner JOIN). Rows with a NULL currency or NULL txn_date are also left out.
3. FX tie-break: rate_date DESC, then fx _row_seq DESC, ranked per source row of the transaction table.
4. daily_rate_eur: ROUND(x, 4, 1) truncates toward zero. This is done with floor for values of 0 or more and ceil for negative values. It looks deliberate, so it is not listed as a defect.
5. monthly_instalment_eur: term_days / 30 is integer division in the legacy code too, and this is kept as is. The divisor is cast to int so the decimal result type matches SQL Server's (decimal(25,13) before ROUND).
6. Spark add_months (Spark 3.0+) does not snap to month end. It therefore gives the same result as SQL Server DATEADD(MONTH) on an EOMONTH date.
7. A term_days of 0 makes the legacy job fail with a divide-by-zero error, and Spark in ANSI mode raises an error the same way.
8. traps_handled is empty because I don't have the trap card ids. The collation handling and integer division are dealt with deliberately in the code.
